# InfoBar

Header: `winui/ui/status/InfoBar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/status/InfoBar.hpp`.

An inline, closable banner that shows an app-wide status message with a severity color and icon.

A freshly built bar is closed: it takes no room and draws nothing until set_open(true). Title, message and the optional action button sit on one line when they fit and stack (wrapping at whole words) when they don't; the bar is at least 48 DIPs tall. Optional custom content ([set_content()](#set_content)) gets a row of its own below them. The [InfoBar](#uiinfobar) itself is never a tab stop. Its action button, its content's controls and its close button are.

Closing runs in a fixed order: a close-button click first raises [on_close_button_click()](#on_close_button_click), then [on_closing()](#on_closing) (return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it open, leaving [is_open()](#is_open) true). Only a close that goes ahead flips [is_open()](#is_open) to false and raises [on_closed()](#on_closed). set_open(false) runs the same [on_closing()](#on_closing) and [on_closed()](#on_closed) sequence with reason Programmatic. Reopening raises nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative, with the open state in a Property:
ui::Property<bool> open{true};
window.set_content(ui::InfoBar{
    .title     = "Update available",
    .message   = "Restart the app to apply the update.",
    .is_open   = open,
    .severity  = ui::InfoBarSeverity::Success,
    .on_closed = [&open](ui::PopupCloseReason) { open = false; },
    .action_button_content = ui::Button{.text = "Restart", .on_click = [] { restart_app(); }},
});

// Imperative:
auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* bar   = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::InfoBarControl>("Offline", "Changes will sync later.",
                                                           ui::InfoBarSeverity::Warning, true));
bar->on_closing([](const ui::PopupClosingArgs& args) {
    return args.reason == ui::PopupCloseReason::Programmatic ? ui::Cancel : ui::Proceed; // keep it open
});
bar->set_action_button_content(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Retry"))->on_click([] { save(); });
```

## `ui::InfoBar`

An inline status banner. Builds a [ui::InfoBarControl](#uiinfobarcontrol). Closed by default, matching the control.

The handlers are installed before [`is_open`](#uiinfobar-is_open) is bound, so a bound [`is_open`](#uiinfobar-is_open) flipping back to false raises [`.on_closing`](#uiinfobar-on_closing)/[`.on_closed`](#uiinfobar-on_closed) like any other close.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> update_ready{true};

window.set_content(ui::InfoBar{
    .title         = "Update available",
    .message       = "Restart to install.",
    .is_open       = update_ready, // two-way: closing the bar writes false
    .severity      = ui::InfoBarSeverity::Success,
    .action_button_content = ui::Button{.text = "Restart", .on_click = [&] { restart_app(); }},
});
```

```cpp
ui::InfoBar{
    .title, .message, .is_open, .severity, .closable, .icon_visible, .style, .margin, .width,
    .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_close_button_click,
    .on_closing, .on_closed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .action_button_content, .content
}
```

## `ui::InfoBarControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

An inline, closable banner that shows an app-wide status message with a severity color and icon.

A freshly built bar is closed: it takes no room and draws nothing until set_open(true). Title, message and the optional action button sit on one line when they fit and stack (wrapping at whole words) when they don't; the bar is at least 48 DIPs tall. Optional custom content ([set_content()](#set_content)) gets a row of its own below them. The [InfoBar](#uiinfobar) itself is never a tab stop. Its action button, its content's controls and its close button are.

Closing runs in a fixed order: a close-button click first raises [on_close_button_click()](#on_close_button_click), then [on_closing()](#on_closing) (return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it open, leaving [is_open()](#is_open) true). Only a close that goes ahead flips [is_open()](#is_open) to false and raises [on_closed()](#on_closed). set_open(false) runs the same [on_closing()](#on_closing) and [on_closed()](#on_closed) sequence with reason Programmatic. Reopening raises nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative, with the open state in a Property:
```

### set_open

```cpp

```

Setting false runs the closing sequence, which [on_closing()](#on_closing) can cancel, with reason Programmatic. Setting true always reopens. Does nothing, and raises nothing, if the value is unchanged.

### is_closable

```cpp

```

Whether the close button shows; true by default.


Shows/hides the owned close button; true by default.

### enabled

```cpp
bool enabled() const
```

A disabled bar grays out its close button, which then takes no input. The action button and the content keep their own state.

### set_action_button_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_action_button_content(std::unique_ptr<T> action)
```

Takes ownership of the action element (normally a [Button](button.md#uibutton), or one with `ButtonVariant::Hyperlink`) and returns a non-owning observer. It sits after the message.

### action_button_content

```cpp
Element* action_button_content() const
```

The action element (non-owning), or nullptr.

### clear_action_button_content

```cpp
void clear_action_button_content()
```

Removes and destroys the action element. Updates the layout.

### set_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_content(std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

Takes ownership of custom content and returns a non-owning observer; a null [`content`](#content) clears it. The content gets the full width between the icon and the close button, on its own row below the title, message and action. With no title, message or action it moves up into their row instead, centered against the icon and close button. The bar never stacks or wraps it as it does the message. The content lays itself out in the width it is given.

### content

```cpp
Element* content() const
```

The custom content (non-owning), or nullptr.

```cpp
void clear_content()
```

Removes and destroys the custom content. Updates the layout.

### on_close_button_click

```cpp
void on_close_button_click(Callback<void()> handler)
```

Fired on every close-button click, before [on_closing()](#on_closing), whether or not the close is then canceled.

### on_closing

```cpp
void on_closing(Callback<Decision(const PopupClosingArgs&)> handler)
```

Runs before [is_open()](#is_open) flips to false. Returning [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) keeps the bar open, and [is_open()](#is_open) stays true throughout.

### on_closed

```cpp
void on_closed(Callback<void(PopupCloseReason)> handler)
```

Fired once a close goes ahead, that is when [on_closing()](#on_closing) did not cancel it.


Every owned child that currently takes part in input, focus and rendering, in tab order: the action, then the custom content, while open; the close button while open and closable.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](../tree/element.md#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

[automation_name()](../tree/element.md#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

At least 48 DIPs tall, taller when the content stacks (see [is_vertical()](#is_vertical)) or custom content adds its row. Zero size while closed.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

## Enumerations

### InfoBarSeverity

```cpp
enum class InfoBarSeverity
```

How serious an [InfoBar](#uiinfobar)'s message is; picks the bar's background color and its status icon.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Informational` | neutral background, info icon (the default) |
| `Success` | success background, check-mark icon |
| `Warning` | caution background, warning icon |
| `Error` | critical background, error icon |
